title: A Systematic Review of Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models: Trends, Taxonomy, Evaluation, Defenses, and Opportunities
explain_beginner: This paper reviews how people can trick large language models, the AI systems behind chatbots and writing tools, by slipping hidden instructions into what they type. The authors gathered many studies and sorted these tricks into groups, from simple word swaps to sneaky multi step conversations and even images. They also looked at ways to test and block such attacks. It matters because these AI systems are now used in many everyday products, so understanding how they can be misled helps builders make them safer and helps everyone trust them more.
explain_business: This review shows that prompt injection is a real and evolving risk for any company deploying large language models, with attacks ranging from simple text tricks to complex multi turn and image based exploits. The authors provide a structured way to classify these attacks by how they manipulate input and what the attacker wants, plus a survey of testing methods and defenses such as input validation, content filtering, and safety training. For executives, this informs decisions about AI risk assessment, vendor evaluation, and where to invest in safeguards before scaling LLM powered products.
explain_practitioner: This systematic review synthesizes prompt injection research, covering attack evolution from natural language overrides to multi turn manipulations, indirect injections via JSON and XML, and tool assisted exploits with automated prompt generation and multi modal inputs. Attacks are taxonomized by manipulation level, character, word, sentence, semantic, and by adversarial intent such as prompt leaking and harmful content generation. The review examines these within varied LLM architectures and applications including machine translation and Chain of Thought reasoning, surveys evaluation benchmarks, datasets, and metrics, and assesses defenses like automated red teaming, input validation, content filtering, and alignment training. It focuses specifically on immediate injection and maps open research gaps.
